item.title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.26922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(\Delta^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $\Delta$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants. A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides with the Kashiwara--Kim--Oh--Park seed of $\Delta^{m-2}$. Hence it is the quantum Grothendieck ring of a monoidal localization, at the frozen modules, of a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(\Delta^{m-2})$ with the same simple objects, and a quantization of the braid variety $X(\Delta^{m-1})$. The whole algebra $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ is a skew Laurent extension of $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ in $(m-1)(n-1)$ frozen variables.
item.dc:creator: Min Huang, Zhihao Wang

item.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
item.description: arXiv:2611.27001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities. But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accumulates semantic debt: definitions and results with unchecked mathematical interpretations are reused as foundations for further work. A library may keep compiling and produce the desired formal theorem while users lose track of which mathematical claims they can responsibly rely on. Reliable reuse is also a prerequisite for Terence Tao's vision of formal mathematics as something people can navigate, explain, learn from, and build with. This paper takes our work connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture as a case study of the challenges of reliable reuse as formal developments scale.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Cheng Guu

item.title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$. Following the method of the result in type $\mathbb{A}$, we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{B}_n}$ is a polynomial ring.
item.dc:creator: Nur Cataltepe

item.title: Simple Yetter-Drinfeld Modules and Extensions over Fractional Infinite-Dimensional Taft Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.27205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra $T=T(\underline m,t,\xi)$, including the infinite-dimensional induced family and the finite-dimensional truncated and cyclic families. We determine their explicit structures and isomorphism criteria, and classify first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules together with their middle modules. We also establish the primary decomposition with respect to $z^t$ and prove that every nonzero-eigenvalue component is wild when $m>1$.
item.dc:creator: Yiwei Zheng

item.title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.27972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enhancement in the sense of Turaev, and the resulting knot invariant is the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant of knots colored by $X$.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Galindo

item.title: The 1-Loop and Ohtsuki-Takata Invariants for Alternating Braids
item.description: arXiv:2611.26790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a step towards resolving the 1-loop conjecture, Ohtsuki and Takata defined their own eponymous invariant in terms of an open knot diagram, and showed that it is equal to the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for two-bridge knots. Garoufalidis and Yoon then showed that the 1-loop invariant is equal to the Ohtsuki-Takata invariant using a technique involving a collapsed octahedral decomposition. This paper expands those techniques to relate the matrix determinants of the 1-loop and Ohtsuki-Takata invariants for the case of reduced alternating braids.
item.dc:creator: Alexander R. Pierson

item.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.27378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Yuma Furuta

item.title: Critical Ising and Temperley-Lieb-Jones States: Cone Haag Duality and the Trivial Algebra Object
item.description: arXiv:2611.27892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the algebra object of two critical Ising states in the operator algebraic framework of fusion category symmetry. The boundary subalgebra is the even part of the Pauli chain, and its DHR category is the toric code. We treat two models. The first is the classical Ising model in two dimensions, through its row transfer matrix. The second is the Ising chain in a transverse field. For the critical transfer matrix state and for the ground state of the critical chain, the algebra object is exactly the tensor unit. In a second part we treat the critical Temperley--Lieb--Jones chains at $\delta=2\cos(\pi/(k+2))$. For every $k\ge2$ the ground state selected by the vacuum block is pure and has trivial algebra object in the Drinfeld centre of the even part. At $k=2$ this recovers the critical Ising chain.
item.dc:creator: David E Evans

item.title: Irreducible representations of pointed Hopf algebras of type $A_2$
item.description: arXiv:2507.21978v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the irreducible representations of a family of finite-dimensional pointed liftings $H_\lambda$ of the Nichols algebra associated with the diagram $A_2$ with parameter $q=-1$. We show that these algebras have infinite representation type and construct an indecomposable $H_\lambda$-module of dimension $n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Finally, we study a semisimple category $\underline{\operatorname{Rep}} H_\lambda$ arising as a quotient of $\operatorname{Rep} H_\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Agust\'in Garc\'ia Iglesias, Alfio Antonio Rodriguez

item.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04232v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Blasco

item.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06616v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A separate package in the repository imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.1, which moves the whole library to Lean v4.35.
item.dc:creator: Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli

item.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2501.04501v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types. To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.
item.dc:creator: Naoki Genra, Thibault Juillard

item.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2611.21654v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Kouno
